d: A data structure that tracks a set of elements partitioned into a number of disjoint (non-overlapping) subsets.

p: Union-Find (Disjoint Set) tracks distinct sets of elements. It is extremely fast for finding if two elements are in the same set, and for merging sets. Path Compression flattens the tree, making it O(1).
1. `find(x)`: recursively find the root parent. Point node directly to root (Path Compression).
2. `union(x, y)`: find roots of x and y. Make the root with higher rank the parent of the other (Union by Rank).

class UnionFind:
  def __init__(self, n):
    self.par = [i for i in range(n)]
    self.rank = [1] * n

  def find(self, n1):
    res = n1
    while res != self.par[res]:
      self.par[res] = self.par[self.par[res]] # Path compression
      res = self.par[res]
    return res

  def union(self, n1, n2):
    p1, p2 = self.find(n1), self.find(n2)
    if p1 == p2: return False
    if self.rank[p1] > self.rank[p2]:
      self.par[p2] = p1
    else:
      self.par[p1] = p2
      self.rank[p2] += self.rank[p1]
    return True
Time: Amortized O(1) (Inverse Ackermann). Space: O(V).

Initial: {A} {B} {C} {D}
Union(A, B): {A, B} {C} {D}
Union(C, D): {A, B} {C, D}
Union(B, C): {A, B, C, D} -> All connected!
